name: Shape
brief: Shape class for creating and manipulating vector graphics paths.
description: Extends `Paint` to inherit transformation and opacity methods.

members.name: moveTo
members.brief: Moves the path cursor to a new point without drawing.
description: This starts a new subpath at the specified coordinates. Subsequent drawing commands will start from this point.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining
examples:
shape.moveTo(100, 100)
     .lineTo(200, 200);

members.name: lineTo
members.brief: Draws a straight line from the current point to the specified coordinates.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: cubicTo
members.signature: cubicTo( cx1: number, cy1: number, cx2: number, cy2: number, x: number, y: number ): this
members.brief: Draws a cubic Bézier curve from the current point to (x, y).

params.name: cx1
params.description: X coordinate of first control point

params.name: cy1
params.description: Y coordinate of first control point

params.name: cx2
params.description: X coordinate of second control point

params.name: cy2
params.description: Y coordinate of second control point

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: close
members.brief: Closes the current subpath by drawing a straight line back to the starting point.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining
examples:
shape.moveTo(100, 50)
     .lineTo(150, 150)
     .lineTo(50, 150)
     .close(); // Completes the triangle

members.name: appendRect
members.signature: appendRect( x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number, options: RectOptions = {} ): this
members.brief: Appends a rectangle path to the shape.
description: Creates a rectangular path with optional rounded corners. Multiple rectangles can be added to the same shape.

params.name: x
params.description: X coordinate of the top-left corner

params.name: y
params.description: Y coordinate of the top-left corner

params.name: options
params.description: Optional corner rounding and path direction

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining
examples:
// Simple rectangle
shape.appendRect(50, 50, 200, 100);

// Rounded rectangle
shape.appendRect(50, 50, 200, 100, { rx: 10, ry: 10 });

members.name: appendCircle
members.signature: appendCircle( cx: number, cy: number, rx: number, ry: number = rx, clockwise: boolean = true ): this
members.brief: Appends a circle or ellipse path to the shape.
description: Creates a circular or elliptical path. If only one radius is provided, creates a perfect circle. If two radii are provided, creates an ellipse.

params.name: ry
params.description: Vertical radius (defaults to rx for perfect circle)

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: appendPath
members.signature: appendPath( commands: readonly PathCommand[], points: ReadonlyArray<readonly number[]> ): this
members.brief: Appends a pre-built path to the shape from raw command and point arrays.
description: This is the low-level counterpart to `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `cubicTo` and `close`. It lets you feed an entire path in a single call, which is useful when the path data already exists in command/point form (e.g. imported from another source or produced by `path`).
Each command consumes points from `points` in order: - `PathCommand.MoveTo` / `PathCommand.LineTo`: 1 point - `PathCommand.CubicTo`: 3 points (control1, control2, end) - `PathCommand.Close`: 0 points
The total number of points consumed by `commands` must equal `points.length`.

params.name: points
params.description: Points as `[x, y]` pairs, consumed in order by the commands

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: path
members.signature: path(): { commands: PathCommand[]; points: Array<[number, number]> }
members.brief: Retrieves the shape's current path as command and point arrays.
description: Returns a snapshot of the path data accumulated by the path-building methods (or `appendPath`). The returned arrays are copies and can be safely modified and fed back into `appendPath`.
members.returns: An object with `commands` (path commands) and `points` ([x, y] tuples)

members.name: fillRule
members.brief: Sets the fill rule for the shape.
description: The fill rule determines how the interior of a shape is calculated when the path intersects itself or when multiple subpaths overlap.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: trimPath
members.signature: trimPath(begin: number, end: number, simultaneous: boolean = true): this
members.brief: Sets the trim of the shape along the defined path segment, controlling which part is visible.
description: This method allows you to trim/cut paths, showing only a portion from the begin to end point. This is particularly useful for animations (e.g., drawing a line progressively) or creating partial shapes like arcs from circles.
If the values exceed the 0-1 range, they wrap around (similar to angle wrapping).

params.name: begin
params.description: Start of the segment to display (0.0 to 1.0, where 0 is the path start)

params.name: end
params.description: End of the segment to display (0.0 to 1.0, where 1 is the path end)

params.name: simultaneous
params.description: How to handle multiple paths within the shape:   - `true` (default): Trimming applied simultaneously to all paths   - `false`: All paths treated as one entity with combined length

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: fill
members.brief: Sets the fill for the shape with a gradient.

params.name: gradient
params.description: LinearGradient or RadialGradient to use as fill

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: fill
members.signature: fill(r: number, g: number, b: number, a?: number): this
members.brief: Sets the fill for the shape with a solid color.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: fill
members.signature: fill( gradientOrR: Fill | number, g?: number, b?: number, a: number = 255 ): this
members.brief: Sets the fill for the shape with either a solid color or gradient.
description: This method supports two calling patterns: 1. Solid color: `fill(r, g, b, a?)` 2. Gradient: `fill(gradient)`

members.name: stroke
members.brief: Sets the stroke width for the shape.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: stroke
members.brief: Sets comprehensive stroke styling options for the shape.

params.name: options
params.description: Stroke configuration including width, color, gradient, caps, joins, and miter limit

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining

members.name: stroke
members.brief: Sets the stroke styling for the shape.
description: This method supports two calling patterns: 1. Simple width: `stroke(width)` 2. Full options: `stroke({ width, color, gradient, cap, join, miterLimit })`

members.name: order
members.brief: Sets the rendering order of the shape's stroke and fill.
description: By default the fill is rendered first and the stroke on top of it. Passing `true` reverses this so the stroke is drawn first and the fill on top — useful when you want the fill to cover the inner half of a thick stroke.

params.name: strokeFirst
params.description: `true` renders the stroke before the fill; `false` (default) renders the stroke on top

members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining
examples:
shape.appendCircle(150, 150, 50)
     .fill(255, 255, 255, 255)
     .stroke({ width: 20, color: [0, 0, 0, 255] })
     .order(true); // stroke under the fill

members.name: reset
members.brief: Resets the shape's path data while retaining fill and stroke properties.
description: This method clears all path commands (moveTo, lineTo, cubicTo, appendRect, etc.) but preserves the shape's fill color, gradient, stroke settings, and transformations. This is useful for animations where you want to redraw the path while keeping the same styling.
members.returns: The Shape instance for method chaining
